words.gloss: of the one with eight qualities

literal: Perception without sense-organ-like quality they-are-without-indeed, eight-qualities-having-one's feet not-bowing head.
translation: A head that does not bow to the feet of the one with eight qualities is as useless as a sense organ without the power of perception.
modern: எட்டு குணங்களை உடைய கடவுளின் திருவடிகளை வணங்காத தலைகள், அறியும் திறன் இல்லாத ஐம்பொறிகளைப் போல எந்தப் பயனும் இல்லாதவை ஆகும்.
explanation: This couplet compares a head that refuses to bow to the divine to a defective sense organ. Just as an eye that cannot see or an ear that cannot hear lacks its defining quality, a head loses its true purpose if it does not show reverence. The phrase eṇkuṇattāṉ refers to the one possessing eight infinite qualities, representing the supreme being. The word kōḷ means the capacity to grasp or perceive, which is the essential function of any sense organ.
